newsitem.title: POLAND: SCHRODER CONSORTIUM TO ADVISE BANK HANDLOWY SALE.
newsitem.headline: SCHRODER CONSORTIUM TO ADVISE BANK HANDLOWY SALE.

text.p: A consortium led by British investment bank J.Henry Schroder & Company Ltd was chosen as the financial adviser in the privatisation of Poland's Bank Handlowy SA, the Polish Treasury Ministry said in a statement.

It said Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz reached an agreement with the British bank and also signed Bank Handlowy's issue prospectus, sending it to the Securities Commission (KPW) in order to get its approval to begin the public offering.
The statement did not give any other details and the treasury ministry was not immidiately available for comment.
Earlier on Thurday Poland modified the privatisation plan for Handlowy to include a convertible bond issue for yet-to-be created pension funds, according to an informed source.

The source, who asked not to be named, said the plan to issue convertible bonds rather than to set aside 30 percent of Handlowy's shares for the prospective funds meant that the size of share tranches had to change to take into account the prospective change in share capital.
The originally planned 30-percent institutional and public offering tranches would be increased to about 42.9 percent of existing shares.
The stakes set aside for the employees and the treasury would rise to 7.1 percent from earlier planned five percent.
The bond issue, when converted into shares would increase the bank's share capital by 30 percent.
Handlowy officials would not comment on the plan and the bank's spokesman said the privatisation scheme would be presented in detail at a news conference next week.
Earlier this week the government said it had cleared Handlowy for sale, with the public offer due in mid-1997, but gave no details of the plan.
